# A window's props are checked in pass2, like every other node's.
#
# They were checked in pass1, because a window at the root of a file is
# *registered* there -- `output(entry = home)` and a sibling window need
# something to resolve against before any body is read. Building the whole
# window at that point checked its arguments against a scope pass1 had not
# finished filling, so a declaration further down the file was not there yet:
#
#     window #home(title = greeting()) { … }
#     func greeting() => "hello"          // undefined: greeting
#
# The same window one level into a component body checked clean, which is the
# tell -- that path is pass2's. Registration reserves a shell now and
# checkWindow reads the rest.
#
# Both files here are the same program, and the second is what made the first
# a bug rather than a rule.

sngl check root.sngl
stdout 'ok'

sngl check nested.sngl
stdout 'ok'

-- root.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

ui.window #home(title=greeting()) {
    ui.text(value="x")
}

func greeting() => "hello"

-- nested.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

component main root {
    ui.window #home(title=greeting()) {
        ui.text(value="x")
    }
}

func greeting() => "hello"

main()
